topics.title: In, on, at for time and place
topics.summary: From big to small: in a month, on a day, at a time.
notice: She lives **in** Istanbul, **on** Bağdat Street, **at** number 12.

compare.note: A means 'at that place' (maybe outside, maybe watching a film). B stresses being inside the building.

explain.en: Time: in for long periods (in 2025, in July, in the morning, in winter); on for days and dates (on Friday, on 5 June, on my birthday); at for exact times and some fixed expressions (at 7:30, at night, at the weekend in British English). Place: in for inside an area or space (in a room, in Turkey); on for surfaces and streets (on the table, on Main Street); at for a point or event (at the bus stop, at work, at a party).
explain.tr: Zaman: in = uzun dönemler, on = gün ve tarih, at = saat. Yer: in = içinde/bölge, on = yüzey/cadde, at = nokta/etkinlik.
explain.ar: الزمن: in للفترات الطويلة (in July, in the morning)، on للأيام والتواريخ (on Friday)، at للساعات وبعض العبارات الثابتة (at 7:30, at night). المكان: in داخل منطقة أو حيّز (in Turkey)، on للأسطح والشوارع (on the table)، at لنقطة أو مناسبة (at the bus stop, at work).

options: I'll wait for you at the bus stop.
I'll wait for you on the bus stop.
exercises.why: A point/place where something happens: at.

exercises.wrong: I'll call you in the evening on 6 o'clock.
answers: I'll call you in the evening at 6 o'clock.
I'll call you at 6 o'clock in the evening.

exercises.wrong: There is a picture in the wall.
answers: There is a picture on the wall.

exercises.answer: The shop closes at six on Saturdays.
alts: On Saturdays the shop closes at six.

exercises.prompt: Write a sentence about when and where you were born. Use in and on or at.
exercises.model: I was born in Bursa on 12 May 2000.

topics.title: Adjectives, adverbs and -ed / -ing adjectives
topics.summary: quick vs. quickly, bored vs. boring.
notice: She is a **careful** driver. She drives **carefully**.
The film was **boring**, so I was **bored**.

compare.note: A means other people find you dull! B means you feel there is nothing interesting to do.

explain.en: Adjectives describe nouns (a quick answer) and come after be, feel, look, seem (You look tired). Adverbs describe verbs: how you do something (answer quickly). Most adverbs = adjective + -ly, but good → well, and fast, hard, late, early stay the same. -ing adjectives describe the thing that causes the feeling (an interesting book); -ed adjectives describe how a person feels (I'm interested).
explain.tr: Sıfat ismi, zarf fiili niteler (good → well). -ing: duyguya sebep olan şey; -ed: kişinin hissettiği.
explain.ar: الصفة تصف الاسم (a quick answer) وتأتي بعد be وfeel وlook وseem (You look tired). الظرف يصف الفعل: كيف تفعل الشيء (answer quickly). معظم الظروف = صفة + -ly، لكن good ← well، وfast وhard وlate وearly لا تتغير. -ing تصف ما يسبب الشعور (an interesting book)، و-ed تصف شعور الشخص (I'm interested).

exercises.prompt: After a long day at work you say:

exercises.wrong: I was very interesting in the lecture.
answers: I was very interested in the lecture.

exercises.why: Hard is already an adverb. 'Hardly' means 'almost not'.
After look (= seem) use an adjective: You look happy.

exercises.answer: The children were excited about the trip.

exercises.prompt: Write a sentence about a film or book you found boring or interesting, and how you felt.
exercises.hint: Use one -ing adjective for the film/book and one -ed adjective for you.
exercises.model: The documentary was fascinating, and I was amazed by the photography.

topics.title: Present perfect with for, since, already, yet, just
notice: Have you finished **yet**? — Yes, I**'ve just** finished.

compare.a: I lived in Paris for two years.
compare.b: I've lived in Paris for two years.
compare.note: A: you don't live there now. B: you still live there.

explain.en: Use the present perfect (have/has + past participle) for situations that started in the past and continue now: for + a period (for three weeks), since + a starting point (since Monday, since 2019). Just = a very short time ago; already = earlier than expected (both go before the participle). Yet = up to now, in questions and negatives, at the end of the sentence.
explain.tr: for + süre, since + başlangıç noktası. just/already fiilden önce, yet olumsuz ve soru cümlesinin sonunda.
explain.ar: المضارع التام (have/has + التصريف الثالث) لوضع بدأ في الماضي ومستمر الآن: for + مدة (for three weeks)، since + نقطة بداية (since 2019). just = قبل قليل، already = أبكر من المتوقع (قبل التصريف الثالث). yet = حتى الآن، في السؤال والنفي وفي آخر الجملة.

exercises.prompt: I've known her ___ we were children.

exercises.why: Started in the past and continues: present perfect.

options: Have you done your homework yet?
Have you done yet your homework?

exercises.why: Yesterday is a finished time: past simple.

exercises.wrong: I work here for three years.
answers: I've worked here for three years.
I have worked here for three years.
I've been working here for three years.
I have been working here for three years.

exercises.prompt: In which sentence does she still teach?
options: She has taught for twenty years.

exercises.why: Just goes between have and the participle.

options: I've been to London last year.
exercises.why: Last year is finished: I went to London last year.

exercises.prompt: How long have you studied English? Answer with for or since.
exercises.model: I've studied English since I was twelve.

topics.title: Past perfect: the earlier past
topics.summary: had + participle when one past event happened before another.
notice: When we arrived, the film **had** already **started**.
She was nervous because she **had** never **flown** before.
I realised I **had left** my keys at home.

compare.a: When I got to the station, the train left.
compare.b: When I got to the station, the train had left.
compare.note: A: the train left as you arrived. B: the train was already gone before you arrived.

explain.en: Use the past perfect (had + past participle) to show that one past action happened before another past action or time. It is common with because, when, by the time, already, never…before, and after verbs like realise, discover, find out. If the order is already clear (with after or before), the past simple is often enough.
explain.tr: Past perfect (had + V3): geçmişteki bir olaydan daha önce olan olay.
explain.ar: الماضي التام (had + التصريف الثالث) يدل على أن حدثاً ماضياً وقع قبل حدث ماضٍ آخر أو وقت ماضٍ. يكثر مع because وwhen وby the time وalready وnever…before وبعد realise وdiscover وfind out. إذا كان الترتيب واضحاً (مع after أو before) يكفي غالباً الماضي البسيط.

exercises.prompt: By the time the police arrived, the thief ___ (escape).
exercises.why: The escape happened before the police arrived.

exercises.prompt: I didn't recognise him because he ___ (change) a lot.
exercises.why: The change happened before the moment of not recognising.

exercises.prompt: In which sentence had the guests gone before she arrived?
options: When she arrived, the guests left.
When she arrived, the guests had left.
I had visited Rome last summer.
exercises.why: One simple past event: past simple.

exercises.wrong: She told me she has lost her passport.
answers: She told me she had lost her passport.
exercises.why: Earlier than 'told' in the past: had lost.

exercises.wrong: It was the first time I ever saw snow.
answers: It was the first time I had ever seen snow.
exercises.why: After 'It was the first time', use the past perfect.

exercises.answer: I realised that I had forgotten my phone.
alts: I realised I had forgotten my phone.

exercises.prompt: The exam was easy because I ___ ...

options: He had never seen the sea before that trip.
When I woke up, it had stopped raining.
Yesterday I had gone to the gym.
exercises.why: No earlier past here: Yesterday I went to the gym.

exercises.prompt: Write about a time you arrived somewhere late. What had already happened?
exercises.model: When I got to the meeting, my manager had already started the presentation.

topics.title: Must, might, can't: how sure are you?
topics.summary: Guessing about the present with modal verbs.
notice: She's not answering. She **might be** asleep.
You've been travelling all day. You **must be** tired.
That **can't be** Ali. He's in Germany.
It **could be** true, but I'm not sure.

compare.note: A: you are almost sure (the lights are on, his car is there). B: it's possible, about 50%.

explain.en: Use must when you are almost certain something is true (You must be hungry). Use might, may or could when it is possible (It may rain later). Use can't when you are almost certain something is not true (That can't be right). Do not use mustn't for this meaning: mustn't means 'it is not allowed'. After a modal, use the base verb (must be, might know).
explain.tr: must = neredeyse eminim (doğru); might/may/could = mümkün; can't = neredeyse eminim (doğru değil). mustn't bu anlamda kullanılmaz.
explain.ar: must = شبه متأكد أن الأمر صحيح (You must be hungry). might/may/could = ممكن (It may rain later). can't = شبه متأكد أنه غير صحيح (That can't be right). لا تستعمل mustn't بهذا المعنى، فهي تعني «ممنوع». بعد الفعل الناقص يأتي الفعل المجرد (must be).

exercises.prompt: Her car isn't here and the lights are off. She ___ at home.
exercises.why: Almost sure it's not true: can't. Mustn't means prohibition.

exercises.prompt: You've won the lottery! You ___ very happy.
Take an umbrella. It ___ rain later. (it's possible)

exercises.wrong: He must to be very rich.
This mustn't be the right address. There's no house here.
answers: This can't be the right address. There's no house here.
This can't be the right address.

options: The keys could be in the car.
The keys must be in the car.

exercises.why: Might be + -ing or might + verb: He might be working late.

exercises.answer: You must be very proud of your son.

exercises.prompt: Someone is knocking. It's 9 p.m. and we're not expecting anyone. It ___ ...
Your friend hasn't replied to your messages all day. Write two guesses: one with might and one with can't or must.
exercises.hint: might/may = possible; must = almost sure; can't = almost sure it's not.
exercises.model: She might be busy at work. She can't be angry with me — we talked yesterday.

topics.title: Verbs and adjectives with prepositions
topics.summary: depend on, interested in, good at: fixed partner words.

compare.note: Listen always needs 'to' before its object. These partner words must be learned as chunks.

explain.en: Many verbs and adjectives are followed by a fixed preposition: depend on, listen to, wait for, look forward to, belong to, apply for, agree with (someone), good at, interested in, afraid of, responsible for, different from, married to. After a preposition, use a noun or the -ing form: I'm good at cooking. Learn them as chunks, not word by word.
explain.tr: Bazı fiil ve sıfatlar sabit edatlarla gelir; parça (chunk) olarak öğren. Edattan sonra isim veya -ing gelir.
explain.ar: أفعال وصفات كثيرة يليها حرف جر ثابت: depend on, listen to, wait for, look forward to, belong to, apply for, agree with, good at, interested in, afraid of, responsible for, different from. بعد حرف الجر يأتي اسم أو صيغة -ing: I'm good at cooking. تعلّمها كقطع كاملة لا كلمة كلمة.

answers: I am not good at sports.
I am interested in learning Spanish.

exercises.why: Discuss has no preposition: discuss the problem.

exercises.answer: She applied for a job in Berlin.

exercises.prompt: Write a sentence about something you are good at and something you are afraid of.
exercises.hint: good at + noun/-ing; afraid of + noun/-ing.
exercises.model: I'm good at drawing, but I'm afraid of speaking in public.
